q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'?
e: Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the father of the Indian Space Programme; he set up INCOSPAR in 1962, the forerunner of ISRO.

q: India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched in the year:
e: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, named after the ancient astronomer, was launched on 19 April 1975 by a Soviet rocket from Kapustin Yar.

q: The first woman to travel into space was:
e: Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union became the first woman to travel into space, in June 1963 aboard the Vostok 6 spacecraft.

q: The highest gallantry award of India conferred for acts of bravery in wartime is the:
e: The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest gallantry award for wartime, given for the most conspicuous bravery in the presence of the enemy; the Ashoka Chakra is the corresponding peacetime award.

q: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the highest national honour in its field, is given for outstanding contribution to:
e: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, instituted in 1969 in the name of the father of Indian cinema, is the highest national honour for lifetime contribution to cinema.

q: Who was the first Indian to win an Academy Award (Oscar)?
e: Bhanu Athaiya was the first Indian to win an Academy Award (Oscar), receiving it for costume design in Richard Attenborough's film 'Gandhi'.

q: The famous Sanskrit play 'Abhijnanashakuntalam' was written by:
e: 'Abhijnanashakuntalam', the celebrated Sanskrit play about King Dushyanta and Shakuntala, was written by the classical poet Kalidasa.

q: 'Long Walk to Freedom' is the autobiography of:
e: 'Long Walk to Freedom' (1994) is the autobiography of Nelson Mandela, the South African leader who fought apartheid and became his country's first black President.

q: The first Indian to win an individual gold medal at the Olympic Games was:
e: Abhinav Bindra was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal, in the 10 metre air rifle event at the Beijing Olympics of 2008.

q: World Environment Day is celebrated every year on:
e: World Environment Day is celebrated on 5 June every year, under the aegis of the United Nations Environment Programme, to spread awareness of environmental protection.

q: Indian Railways was nationalised in the year:
e: Indian Railways was nationalised in 1951, when the Government of India took over the remaining company-managed railway systems into one State-owned network.

q: The Railway Board was constituted in 1905 on the recommendations of the:
e: The Railway Board was constituted in 1905 on the recommendations of the Robertson Committee, which had inquired into railway administration and finance.

q: Which train, started in 1866 as the 'East Indian Railway Mail', is among the oldest running trains of India?
e: The Kalka Mail, started in 1866 as the 'East Indian Railway Mail' between Howrah and Delhi, is among the oldest running trains of India.

q: The Deccan Queen is credited with being the first train in India to introduce:
e: The Deccan Queen of 1930 is credited with being the first train in India to have vestibuled coaches, that is, coaches connected by flexible covered gangways.

q: The first double-decker train service in India, introduced in 1978 as the Sinhagad Express, ran between:
e: India's first double-decker train service was the Sinhagad Express, introduced in 1978 between Mumbai and Pune.

q: The second Rajdhani Express, introduced in 1972, connected New Delhi with:
e: The second Rajdhani Express, introduced in 1972 after the Howrah Rajdhani of 1969, connected New Delhi with Mumbai (Bombay Central).

q: The longest daily train service in India by distance is the:
e: Among daily trains, the Kerala Express between New Delhi and Thiruvananthapuram covers the longest distance; the still longer Vivek Express is not a daily service.

q: The Train 18 (Vande Bharat) trainsets were designed and manufactured at:
e: The Train 18 trainsets, later named Vande Bharat Express, were designed and manufactured at the Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai.

q: The first locomotive rolled out by Chittaranjan Locomotive Works in 1950 was named:
e: The first locomotive rolled out by the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works in 1950 was a steam locomotive named 'Deshbandhu', after Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das.

q: India's most powerful locomotive, the 12,000 HP WAG-12, is assembled at:
e: India's most powerful locomotive, the 12,000 HP WAG-12 electric locomotive, is assembled at the electric locomotive factory at Madhepura in Bihar.

q: The first railway bridge in India was built across the:
e: The first railway bridge in India was built across Thane Creek, to carry the Bori Bunder to Thane line of 1853 over the creek.

q: The oldest railway station in India still in operation is:
e: Royapuram station in Chennai, opened in 1856 on the first line of South India, is the oldest railway station in India still in operation.

q: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Victoria Terminus), Mumbai, was designed by the architect:
e: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (formerly Victoria Terminus), Mumbai, was designed by the British architect Frederick William Stevens in the Victorian Gothic style.

q: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in the year:
e: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Victoria Terminus) was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2004 for its outstanding Victorian Gothic architecture.

q: The original Pamban Bridge, India's first sea bridge, was opened in the year:
e: The original Pamban Bridge, India's first sea bridge connecting Rameswaram island with the mainland, was opened to traffic in 1914.

q: The Konkan Railway line was fully opened to traffic in the year:
e: The Konkan Railway line along the west coast, from Roha to Thokur, was fully opened to traffic in 1998.

q: The Roll-on Roll-off (Ro-Ro) service, carrying loaded trucks on railway wagons, was pioneered in India by:
e: The Roll-on Roll-off (Ro-Ro) service, under which loaded trucks are carried on flat railway wagons, was pioneered in India by the Konkan Railway.

q: The longest tunnel on the Kalka-Shimla Railway is the:
e: The Barog Tunnel is the longest tunnel on the Kalka-Shimla narrow-gauge railway; it is named after Colonel Barog, the engineer associated with its construction.

q: Which railway station is situated half in Maharashtra and half in Gujarat?
e: Navapur railway station is situated half in Maharashtra and half in Gujarat, the inter-State border passing through the station premises.

q: The longest railway station name in India is:
e: Venkatanarasimharajuvaripeta, a station in Andhra Pradesh near the Tamil Nadu border, has the longest railway station name in India.

q: The shortest railway station name in India is:
e: 'Ib', a station in Odisha named after the Ib river, has the shortest railway station name in India, of only two letters.

q: The largest railway junction in India, with lines radiating in seven directions, is:
e: Mathura Junction is regarded as the largest railway junction in India, with railway lines radiating from it in seven directions.

q: The Firozpur division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Firozpur division, covering the border districts of Punjab, is a division of Northern Railway.

q: The Asansol division is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Asansol division, an important coal-belt division in West Bengal, is a part of Eastern Railway.

q: The Bhusawal division belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Bhusawal division, one of the busiest divisions for freight movement, belongs to Central Railway, headquartered at Mumbai.

q: The headquarters of the Railway Rates Tribunal is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Railway Rates Tribunal, which adjudicates complaints relating to railway freight rates, is located at Chennai.

q: The Commission of Railway Safety, which inquires into serious railway accidents, functions administratively under the:
e: The Commission of Railway Safety, which inquires into serious railway accidents, functions administratively under the Ministry of Civil Aviation, so that its inquiries remain independent of the Railway Ministry.

q: The Railway Protection Force is governed by the RPF Act enacted in the year:
e: The Railway Protection Force is governed by the Railway Protection Force Act enacted in 1957 for the protection of railway property and passengers.

q: The working of Indian Railways is presently governed by the:
e: The working of Indian Railways is presently governed by the Railways Act, 1989, which replaced the Indian Railways Act of 1890.

q: The National Academy of Indian Railways (NAIR) at Vadodara was earlier known as the:
e: The National Academy of Indian Railways (NAIR) at Vadodara was earlier known as the Railway Staff College, the premier institute for the training of railway officers.

q: The first train in India to be operated by IRCTC as a 'private' operator, in 2019, was the:
e: The Lucknow-New Delhi Tejas Express, started in October 2019, was the first train of Indian Railways to be operated by IRCTC as a private operator.

q: The first railway station in India to offer free Wi-Fi facility, in 2016, was:
e: Mumbai Central station became the first railway station in India to offer free Wi-Fi facility, in January 2016, under the RailTel-Google project.

q: Internet-based railway ticket booking (e-ticketing) through IRCTC was launched in the year:
e: Internet-based railway ticket booking (e-ticketing) through IRCTC was launched in August 2002, enabling passengers to book reserved tickets online.

q: 'Rail Neer', the packaged drinking water supplied on trains and at stations, is a brand of:
e: 'Rail Neer' is the brand of packaged drinking water produced and supplied by IRCTC at railway stations and on trains.

q: The eco-friendly bio-toilets used in Indian Railways coaches were developed in association with:
e: The eco-friendly bio-toilets fitted in railway coaches were developed by Indian Railways in association with DRDO, adapting its biodigester technology.

q: Before becoming a cricketer, M. S. Dhoni worked with Indian Railways as a:
e: Before rising in cricket, M. S. Dhoni worked with Indian Railways as a Travelling Ticket Examiner (TTE) posted at Kharagpur station.

q: Lal Bahadur Shastri resigned as Railway Minister in 1956, taking moral responsibility for the train accident at:
e: Lal Bahadur Shastri resigned as Railway Minister in 1956, accepting moral responsibility for the train accident at Ariyalur in Tamil Nadu.

q: The first woman to become the Chairman of the Railway Board, in 2023, was:
e: Jaya Varma Sinha became the first woman to head the Railway Board, taking over as its Chairman and Chief Executive Officer in 2023.

q: The first 'Kisan Rail' service of Indian Railways, introduced in 2020, ran between:
e: The first 'Kisan Rail' service, run in 2020 for carrying perishable farm produce, operated between Devlali in Maharashtra and Danapur in Bihar.

q: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor has been designed to permit the running of:
e: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor has been designed with higher clearances and axle loads so as to permit the running of double-stack container trains.

q: Driverless (unattended) train operations on the Delhi Metro were first introduced on the:
e: Delhi Metro began unattended (driverless) train operations on the Magenta Line (Janakpuri West to Botanical Garden) in December 2020, its first line to run in full driverless mode.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. MEMU stands for Mainline Electric Multiple Unit.
2. DEMU stands for Diesel Electric Multiple Unit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: MEMU stands for Mainline Electric Multiple Unit and DEMU stands for Diesel Electric Multiple Unit; both are self-propelled multiple-unit train sets used on Indian Railways.

q: In the locomotive class WDM-3A, the letter 'D' indicates:
e: In Indian Railways locomotive classification, the second letter denotes the power source, so 'D' in WDM-3A indicates diesel traction (W is broad gauge and M is mixed traffic).

q: The Real Time Train Information System (RTIS), used for automatic tracking of trains, was developed by Indian Railways in collaboration with:
e: The Real Time Train Information System (RTIS), which automatically tracks train movements using satellite-based positioning, was developed by Indian Railways in collaboration with ISRO.

q: The 'Amrit Bharat Express' trains introduced by Indian Railways are:

options.A: Non-AC push-pull trains with locomotives at both ends, meant for long-distance travel

e: Amrit Bharat Express trains are non-AC push-pull trains with a locomotive at each end, designed to give long-distance passengers faster and more comfortable travel at affordable fares.

q: The power and procedure for amendment of the Constitution of India is laid down in:
e: Article 368 of the Constitution lays down both the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure to be followed for such amendments.

q: Part II of the Constitution of India deals with:
e: Part II of the Constitution (Articles 5 to 11) deals with citizenship, covering citizenship at commencement, rights of migrants and Parliament's power to regulate citizenship by law.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds office for a term of:

options.A: Five years or until the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
options.B: Four years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
options.C: Six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
options.D: Six years or until the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier

e: Under the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the Comptroller and Auditor General holds office for six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.

q: The Vice-President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

options.A: Elected members of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies
options.B: Members of the Lok Sabha only
options.C: Members of the Rajya Sabha only
options.D: Members of both Houses of Parliament

e: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members; State Legislatures take no part in this election.

q: A Judge of a High Court in India retires at the age of:
e: A Judge of a High Court retires at the age of 62 years; the age was raised from 60 to 62 by the Constitution (Fifteenth Amendment) Act, 1963.

q: The President of India is elected by the system of:

options.C: Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote

e: The President of India is elected in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, as provided in Article 55.

q: The Contingency Fund of India is established under which Article of the Constitution?
e: The Contingency Fund of India is established under Article 267 of the Constitution and is placed at the disposal of the President to meet unforeseen expenditure.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President of India nominates twelve members to the Rajya Sabha from amongst persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art and social service.
2. The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: under Article 80 the President nominates twelve members to the Rajya Sabha for distinction in literature, science, art and social service, and the elected members are chosen by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.

q: The procedure for the impeachment of the President of India has been borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: The procedure for impeachment of the President under Article 61 has been borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.

q: Which was the first Act by which the British Parliament sought to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India?
e: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first Act by which the British Parliament sought to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India; it created the office of Governor-General of Bengal.

q: The system of 'Subsidiary Alliance' was introduced by:
e: The Subsidiary Alliance system, under which Indian rulers kept British troops and accepted a British Resident, was introduced by Lord Wellesley during his Governor-Generalship (1798-1805).

q: The Revolt of 1857 first broke out at:
e: The Revolt of 1857 first broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857, when sepoys mutinied and marched to Delhi.

q: Which Mauryan ruler is believed to have embraced Jainism in the later years of his life?
e: Chandragupta Maurya, founder of the Mauryan empire, is believed to have embraced Jainism in his later years, abdicated the throne and spent his last days at Shravanabelagola with the Jain monk Bhadrabahu.

q: The Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeshwara) Temple at Thanjavur was built by:
e: The Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeshwara) Temple at Thanjavur, a masterpiece of Chola architecture completed around 1010 CE, was built by Rajaraja Chola I.

q: In the Battle of Saraighat (1671), the Ahom forces that defeated the Mughals were commanded by:
e: In the Battle of Saraighat (1671) on the Brahmaputra, the Ahom forces that defeated the Mughals were commanded by the Ahom general Lachit Borphukan.

q: The Brahmo Samaj was founded by:
e: The Brahmo Samaj, a reform movement opposing idolatry and social evils, was founded in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

q: The Servants of India Society was founded by:
e: The Servants of India Society, which trained workers for social and public service, was founded in 1905 by Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

q: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) decided the Anglo-French struggle for supremacy in India in favour of the:
e: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760), in which Sir Eyre Coote defeated the French under Count Lally, decided the Anglo-French struggle for supremacy in India in favour of the British.

q: The book 'Satyarth Prakash' was written by:
e: 'Satyarth Prakash', the principal work setting out the doctrines of the Arya Samaj, was written by its founder, Swami Dayananda Saraswati.

q: The capital of King Harshavardhana was at:
e: King Harshavardhana made Kannauj his capital, shifting it from Thanesar; Kannauj became the centre of power in northern India during his reign.

q: The Kakori train robbery of 1925 is associated with:
e: The Kakori train robbery of August 1925, carried out by revolutionaries of the Hindustan Republican Association to seize Government funds, is associated with Ram Prasad Bismil, one of its principal leaders.

q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
e: The Kosi is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its frequent devastating floods and repeated changes of course in north Bihar.

q: The Sambhar Lake, the largest inland salt lake of India, is located in the State of:
e: The Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is the largest inland salt lake of India and a major source of salt production.

q: The Harappan site of Lothal is famous for its:
e: The Harappan site of Lothal in Gujarat is famous for its artificial dockyard, evidence of maritime trade of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

q: The Rohtang Pass connects the Kullu valley with:
e: The Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh connects the Kullu valley with the Lahaul and Spiti valleys across the Pir Panjal range.

q: The largest tributary of the river Ganga is the:
e: The Yamuna is the largest tributary of the Ganga by length and discharge, joining it at Prayagraj.

q: The Ranthambore National Park is located in the State of:
e: The Ranthambore National Park, famous for its tiger population, is located in the Sawai Madhopur district of Rajasthan.

q: The Valley of Flowers National Park is located in the State of:
e: The Valley of Flowers National Park, known for its alpine meadows and endemic flora, is located in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Krishna river rises near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.
2. The Kaveri river rises at Talakaveri in Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra, and the Kaveri rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Karnataka.

q: The Indian Standard Time is calculated on the basis of which longitude?
e: Indian Standard Time is reckoned from the standard meridian of 82.5 degrees East longitude, which passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.

q: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was established in the year:
e: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the regulator of the securities market, was established in 1988 and was given statutory status in 1992.

q: The headquarters of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), which administers global trade rules, is located at Geneva in Switzerland.

q: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) refers to:

options.A: The rate at which the Reserve Bank lends to commercial banks
options.B: The rate at which banks lend to the general public
options.C: The minimum rate of interest fixed by the Reserve Bank for savings deposits
options.D: The percentage of a bank's deposits which it is required to keep as cash reserve with the Reserve Bank

e: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the percentage of a bank's total deposits which it is required to maintain as cash reserve with the Reserve Bank of India.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Primary deficit is equal to the fiscal deficit minus interest payments.
2. Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments, and revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.

q: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
e: Mars is called the 'Red Planet' because iron oxide (rust) dust on its surface gives it a distinct reddish appearance.

q: A hydrometer is an instrument used to measure the:
e: A hydrometer is an instrument used to measure the relative density (specific gravity) of liquids.

q: The electron was discovered by:
e: The electron, the negatively charged sub-atomic particle, was discovered by J. J. Thomson in 1897 through his cathode ray experiments.

q: The disease beriberi is caused by the deficiency of:
e: Beriberi is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin B1 (thiamine) in the diet.

q: Myopia (short sight) in the human eye is corrected by the use of:
e: Myopia or short sight, in which distant objects appear blurred, is corrected by a concave (diverging) lens, which spreads the rays so that the image falls on the retina.

q: The SI unit of power is the:
e: The SI unit of power is the Watt, named after James Watt; one watt equals one joule per second.

q: The Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, was instituted in the year:
e: The Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, was instituted on 2 January 1954.

q: The book 'A Brief History of Time' was authored by:
e: 'A Brief History of Time', the best-selling book explaining cosmology for general readers, was authored by the physicist Stephen Hawking.

q: The Durand Cup is associated with the game of:
e: The Durand Cup, one of the oldest football tournaments in the world, first played in 1888, is associated with football.

q: National Science Day is celebrated in India every year on:
e: National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February every year to commemorate the discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C. V. Raman on that day in 1928.

q: The Saraswati Samman is awarded for outstanding achievement in the field of:
e: The Saraswati Samman, instituted by the K. K. Birla Foundation, is awarded for outstanding literary work in any of the languages of the Eighth Schedule.
